prompt:
Warm editorial ink-and-wash illustration on a warm cream ground: a loose confident ink line with soft transparent washes over it, muted earth palette of cream, rust, ochre, mustard, sage and warm grey, quiet and hand-made, the register of a good picture book rather than a comic. Object reference: THE THROWING ARM, a hand-made paper-plane launcher that two children plainly built themselves out of scrap. ONE UPRIGHT POST of pale timber about sixty centimetres tall, C-CLAMPED to the end of a wooden workbench. Through the top of the post runs a bolt, and on that bolt swings ONE HINGED ARM of pale wood about as long as a forearm. At the pivot there is ONE VISIBLE COILED STEEL SPRING. At the tip of the arm, a SMALL CRADLE OF CORK AND BENT WIRE grips a folded paper plane by its keel. A WOODEN CLOTHES-PEG TRIGGER hangs on a loop of string. There are pencil marks on the wood and one stray screw. Shown from a front three-quarter angle against a plain cream background. RENDER EXACTLY ONE STATE: the arm is DRAWN BACK and held by the peg, the spring visibly compressed, the plane seated in the cradle, everything still. The arm must NOT also appear swung forward anywhere in the picture. It is ENTIRELY MECHANICAL: NO motor, NO wires, NO cables, NO electronics, NO dials, NO gauges, NO screens, NO glow, NO buttons. Render ONE single image only. This is NOT a contact sheet, NOT a grid, NOT a multi-panel study sheet, NOT a turnaround strip. No panel borders, no captions, no labels, no annotation text of any kind. ABSOLUTELY NOT, these are the rejected poles of this style and any of them is a failure: neon, 3D or CGI or Pixar rendering, glossy plastic, HUD or arc-reactor comic vocabulary, neo-comic styling, photorealism, airbrushing, lens flare, heavy drop shadows.

DEVICE ANATOMY, NON-NEGOTIABLE: any phone, laptop, tablet or monitor is anatomically correct. The GLOWING DISPLAY is on the SCREEN side, and that side FACES ITS USER. A person looking at a device sees its screen; the viewer therefore sees the device's BACK or EDGE plus the light it throws onto the user's face and hands. NEVER put the screen image on the back of a phone, on a laptop's outer lid, or on a monitor's rear. NEVER show a screen facing the camera while the person using it looks at the opposite side. If both the user's face and the screen content must be visible, shoot it over the user's shoulder.

READABLE SURFACES FACE THEIR READER: any book, page, letter, scroll or sign a character is reading or writing faces THAT CHARACTER, never the camera. Compose over-the-shoulder or from behind so the surface genuinely faces them. Any handwriting is abstract handwriting-like line work with NO real readable letters.

NO USER INTERFACE ANYWHERE: no windows, menu bars, buttons, icons, toolbars, panels, form fields, cursors, floating rectangles or screenshot-like elements. Screens carry only soft glow or vague painterly shapes.
